findings.title: Hung spawned flusher processes are not killed before replacement
findings.body: The workers are always created from `multiprocessing.get_context("spawn")`, producing `SpawnProcess` instances. On Linux, `multiprocessing.Process` refers to the default fork-context process class, so a `SpawnProcess` is not an instance of it. Consequently, when a worker is declared hung, this guard skips `process.kill()` and immediately starts a replacement. The old hung worker can remain alive and continue using Redis/Kafka concurrently with its replacement, leaking workers and potentially causing duplicate or competing flushes. The same incorrect type test at line 346 also prevents forcibly terminating a still-running spawned worker during `join`. Check against the multiprocessing base-process type or invoke `kill`/`terminate` based on capability instead.

findings.title: Negative flusher process counts crash initialization
findings.body: `--flusher-processes` accepts any integer, but a negative value is passed through as `max_processes`. `min(negative_value, shard_count)` makes `num_processes` negative, creates an empty process map, and then the shard-distribution loop indexes `self.process_to_shards_map[process_index]`, raising `KeyError` for the first assigned shard. Zero is also silently converted to the default by `max_processes or ...`, rather than being rejected or honored. Validate this CLI option as a positive integer (and validate programmatic construction similarly) before computing the process map.
